submission.justification:
Best unirradiated single-hit resolution among the three technologies. Simulated resolutions (100k events each): T2 at 100/130/150/170/200 um gave 6.29/6.02/5.81/6.02/6.21 um, so 150 um is the best sampled point. T3 (100 um) gave 8.84 um and T1 (100 and 150 um) gave 14.4 and 14.2 um. This matches the 2025 summary (T2 6.0, T3 9.0, T1 14.0 um at 150 um). The goal is resolution, so T2 at 150 um is the performance pick. However, the radiation-suitability constraint is NOT verified for T2. No project document gives irradiated performance or fluence tolerance for any candidate, and the simulation tool only models unirradiated sensors. The only radiation-related hint is that T1 is a 3D-electrode design, which is generally considered more radiation tolerant, but I have no project data confirming this either. Before this recommendation is finalized, T2 must be shown to meet the innermost-layer fluence requirement (irradiated charge collection and resolution). If it cannot, the fallback is T1 (3D), which is expected to be more radiation tolerant but has about 2.4x worse unirradiated resolution (about 14 um). Cooling (CO2 at -35 C) and readout compatibility (50x50 um pixels, all candidates bump-bondable) do not distinguish the options.</justification>
